description: Make CLI, Server, and Runner updates use one authoritative source identity and a verified managed runtime release.

tasks.title: Make source identity authoritative across update scopes
tasks.description: Add an immutable UpdateSourceContext, materialize a read-only snapshot of the resolved revision, allocate transaction-owned writable build/candidate roots, and route full, CLI, Server, and Runner updates through one normalized source resolver. Persist that context in a transaction record before CLI self-update and resume continuation by transaction ID so later stages cannot re-resolve a different root or revision.
acceptanceCriteria: Explicit roots are normalized to absolute paths, default roots are resolved once, and dry-run/human output distinguishes the selection mode, root, and target revision.

Missing, unusable, dirty, revision-less, unsnapshotable, or unwritable-root inputs fail before any managed service target is stopped or replaced and report the selected root, target revision, and failure reason.

Server, web, Runner, and CLI builds read source files only from SnapshotRoot and write intermediates, generated metadata, web output, and candidate artifacts only under BuildWorkspaceRoot or CandidateRoot; the snapshot marker and source digest remain unchanged.

The continuation process loads the original source context and transaction state by ID, including SnapshotRoot, BuildWorkspaceRoot, CandidateRoot, and recovery CLI path after the CLI executable has been replaced.
A legacy CLI without the transaction schema returns bootstrap_required before replacing the CLI, stopping a service, or changing active.json; the supported bootstrap handoff is explicit and tested.

Focused CLI tests cover explicit/default roots, invalid source failure ordering, single revision resolution, immutable snapshot creation, source mutation during build, write-boundary enforcement, bootstrap refusal, dry-run reporting, and continuation argument/state propagation using fake command and filesystem boundaries.
tasks.output: UpdateSourceContext, source resolver, durable transaction record, and continuation wiring in packages/cli.
tasks.notes: Keep source selection and transaction serialization rules in one authority; do not implement a parallel server-side transaction store.

tasks.title: Publish and activate versioned managed runtime artifacts
tasks.description: Implement the managed runtime store and release-oriented artifact builder for Server, web, Runner, and CLI outputs. Keep the source snapshot read-only, stage a self-contained Runner dependency closure, and extend both service-installer backends to use stable absolute launchers and atomically activate a complete RuntimeTargetSet from a candidate release while preserving data roots and credentials outside the release.
acceptanceCriteria: A successful full build creates an isolated release directory containing release.json plus the required Server, web, Runner, and CLI artifacts, with one canonical source revision/version/release identity recorded for the set; component builds retain untouched active entries.

Server and web publishing read from the immutable snapshot but write MSBuild, web, generated metadata, and publish output only to transaction-owned roots; Runner metadata uses the transaction identity and an explicit output path rather than source-tree git discovery.

The managed Runner release contains its runtime package.json, compiled dist, all lockfile-resolved production dependencies, and a dependency manifest that does not resolve through the source worktree or workspace node_modules.
A Server, Runner, or required metadata failure leaves the previous active release and service target unchanged and never exposes a partial candidate as active.

The Linux runtime root is $HOME/.local/share/mohist/runtime and the Windows runtime root is %LOCALAPPDATA%/Mohist/runtime; both installer backends use stable absolute launchers that resolve one atomically replaced active target record.

Artifact-store, snapshot write-boundary, dependency-closure, active-record, build-command, release-manifest, systemd-rendering, Windows-launcher, and source-removal tests use fake process/filesystem boundaries and verify the release starts without the source worktree or workspace dependencies.
tasks.output: ManagedRuntimeStore, RuntimeArtifactBuilder, RuntimeTargetSet activation APIs, release manifests, dependency closure, and platform installer coverage.
tasks.notes: Use versioned release directories and atomic metadata updates; do not overwrite the active artifact in place.

tasks.title: Expose and enforce runtime release identity
tasks.description: Introduce the shared RuntimeIdentity contract and canonical release identity generation, expose artifact-owned release/source identity from Server, Runner, and CLI runtime readback, and bind Runner checks to the exact active connection. Make RuntimeConsistencyValidator compare actual processes with the candidate manifest, treating missing, stale, ambiguous, or mismatched required identities as failures rather than warnings, with explicit full/component scope semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: Server health/system-info, Runner identity, and the exact `mo runtime identity --json` CLI command expose one machine-readable object with component, version, sourceRevision, and releaseId from artifact-owned metadata without reading the source worktree; missing or malformed metadata fails closed.

The canonical identity uses the normalized full source revision, version `0.0.0+<sourceRevision>`, and release ID `mohist-full-<sourceRevision>` or `mohist-<scope>-<sourceRevision>`; package/assembly compatibility versions and timestamps do not alter it.

The CLI publish step compiles the candidate sourceRevision and releaseId into generated identity metadata in the isolated artifact, Server rejects environment-only identity, and Runner readback requires the exact active runnerId and connectionGeneration.
The expected identity is loaded from the candidate release and remains fixed even when the current working directory or source HEAD differs during verification.

A full `mo update` requires matching CLI, Server, and Runner identities; `mo update cli`, `mo update server`, and `mo update runner` verify exactly their activated scope plus any component they actually restart or rely on, and report untouched components without claiming global consistency.
Missing identity, an online Runner without artifact identity, a stale connection generation, or any source/release mismatch produces a nonzero failure and no normal success message.

Server, Runner, CLI, validator, canonical identity, stale-artifact, wrong-connection, matching, mismatched, unavailable, wrong-root, every operation scope, and dry-run tests use injected HTTP, process, filesystem, and time seams.
tasks.output: RuntimeIdentity production/readback fields and strict RuntimeConsistencyValidator plus Server/Runner/CLI tests.
tasks.notes: Readiness and auxiliary asset checks may retain advisory semantics, but required identity checks must be fail-closed.

tasks.title: Coordinate activation, commit, and rollback as one transaction
tasks.description: Implement RuntimeActivationCoordinator and RuntimeTransactionReconciler and integrate them with full and component-specific SourceCodeUpdater flows. Persist explicit transaction states and write-ahead target/slot snapshots, atomically publish complete active-target records, verify candidates, and recover deterministically after build, restart, identity, cancellation, crash, bootstrap, or CLI-continuation failures.
acceptanceCriteria: The transaction records Prepared, CandidateStaged, CandidateActivated, Verifying, Committed, RollingBack, RolledBack, NoVerifiedRuntime, or RecoveryFailed states with candidate and previous target-set, service-unit, CLI-slot, scope, and identity facts.
A candidate that passes all required checks becomes the active last verified release; a build or installation failure before activation leaves the previous target unchanged.
A post-activation failure restores and verifies the previous managed release and service targets when one exists, while the command still returns failure and does not print success.

When no verified release exists, the candidate is stopped or disabled, active.json is atomically set to status none with no target, and the result is reported as no verified runtime; failed restoration performs the same physical quarantine, preserves transaction/candidate paths for diagnosis, and reports recovery failure with an actionable next step.

The complete candidate active-target record is published through one atomic file replacement only after CandidateStaged is durable; stable launchers resolve that record so partial Server/Runner unit writes cannot define a mixed full-update target set.

The reconciler runs before a new update and on managed startup, invokes the recorded recovery CLI slot rather than an unverified candidate, resolves every nonterminal record, rejects concurrent updates while one is unresolved, and bounds recovery/readiness polling with injected TimeProvider-driven deadlines.

A legacy CLI returns bootstrap_required without replacing itself or changing runtime state, while a bootstrapped transaction carries enough state to recover after a crash before or after candidate CLI-slot replacement or partial service activation.

UpdateAll, CLI-only, Server-only, Runner-only, cancellation, build failure, readiness timeout, identity mismatch, kill points after Server/Runner unit and CLI-slot side effects, rollback success, rollback failure with active-target quarantine, crash reconciliation, legacy bootstrap, and no-previous-release tests verify command order, service state, exit codes, and cleanup through fake boundaries.
tasks.output: RuntimeActivationCoordinator and integrated full/component update state machine with rollback and recovery tests.
tasks.notes: Replace the current Runner-only recovery decision path rather than adding a second independent rollback mechanism.

tasks.title: Report target, observed, and migration outcomes
tasks.description: Add a single UpdateReport/output contract for explicit/default source mode, target identity, observed identities, operation scope, failed stage, and recovery result. Make the entire Server update surface projection-only, quarantine legacy web jobs, project authoritative CLI facts into server status/consistency surfaces, preserve non-mutating dry-run behavior, and document the breaking migration from source-bound service units.
acceptanceCriteria: Successful output distinguishes default versus explicit source selection and shows the effective root and target revision/release identity.
Failure output distinguishes unavailable from mismatched identities, names expected and observed values, reports the failed stage and recovery state, and never emits the normal success message.
CLI outcome payloads and server update/consistency responses preserve target, observed, source-mode, and recovery facts without making server persistence authoritative for local activation.

POST `/api/system/update` returns HTTP 409 with `UpdateMutationOwnedByCli` and performs no build, restart, active-target, or CLI-slot mutation; GET status and consistency reads also perform no command, service, lock, or job-advancement side effect.
Persisted running or waiting-for-reconnect web jobs are marked rejected with `UpdateMutationOwnedByCli` on Server startup, their web lock is released, and no background web update is resumed.

Output and tests implement the explicit matrix for `mo update`, `mo update cli`, `mo update server`, and `mo update runner`, including required identities, rollback scope, untouched components, and global versus component-scoped success claims.
Dry-run output lists planned source, artifact, activation, and verification checks without building, mutating service targets, or claiming any runtime is verified.
Legacy source-bound unit detection and operator guidance explain the supported managed-service migration, retained data/credentials, and manual recovery action for custom units.

Focused output, CLI outcome, server route/status/consistency, stale-job startup, dry-run, migration-diagnostic, operation-matrix, bootstrap, and documentation checks assert exact failure/success semantics and preserve the existing fake-boundary test policy.
tasks.output: UpdateReport, CLI/server outcome projection changes, migration diagnostics, and operator-facing update documentation.
tasks.notes: Keep server-side update status a projection of CLI-reported facts and runtime readback; do not move local transaction authority into the web job.
